ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Given the parabola $y=ax^{2}-3ax-4a$ intersects the x-axis at points $A$ and $B$ (with $A$ to the left of $B$) and intersects the negative y-axis at point $C$. Let $P$ be a point on the parabola in the fourth quadrant. If $a=1$, a line through point $P$ is drawn perpendicular to the x-axis, intersecting line segment $BC$ at point $Q$. Find the maximum value of the line segment $PQ$ and the coordinates of point $P$ at this time.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: \textbf{Solution:} When $a=1$, the parabola is $y=x^{2}-3x-4$. By substituting the coordinates of points $B(4,0)$ and $C(0,-4)$ into the expression of the linear function, we obtain the equation of line $BC$ as: $y=x-4$. Let point $P$ be $(t,t^{2}-3t-4)$, then point $Q$ is $(t,t-4)$, $\therefore PQ=(t-4)-(t^{2}-3t-4)=-t^{2}+4t=-(t-2)^{2}+4$, $\therefore$ when $t=2$, $PQ$ reaches its maximum value $\boxed{4}$, at which point $P$ is $\boxed{(2,-6)}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Given the parabola $y=ax^{2}-3ax-4a$ intersects the x-axis at points $A$ and $B$ (with $A$ to the left of $B$) and intersects the negative y-axis at point $C$. Let $P$ be a point on the parabola in the fourth quadrant. If $a=1$, a line through point $P$ is drawn perpendicular to the x-axis, intersecting line segment $BC$ at point $Q$. Find the maximum value of the line segment $PQ$ and the coordinates of point $P$ at this time.
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: When $a=1$, the parabola is $y=x^{2}-3x-4$. Since $B=(4,0)$ and $C=(0,-4)$, line $BC$ is $y=x-4$. Let $P=(t,t^{2}-3t-4)$, then $Q=(t,t-4)$, so $PQ=(t-4)-(t^{2}-3t-4)=-t^{2}+4t=-(t-2)^{2}+4$. Therefore, the maximum value of $PQ$ is $4$ when $t=2$, and at that time $P=(2,-6)$.
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: In the image, it can be seen that the parabola intersects the x-axis at the left point A and the right point B, and intersects the negative y-axis at C. P is in the fourth quadrant. Through P draw a line perpendicular to the x-axis, intersecting segment BC at Q; therefore PQ is the vertical distance between BC and the parabola under the same abscissa. Calculate by the analytic method: when a=1, the parabola is y=x^2-3x-4. Let y=0, obtaining x^2-3x-4=(x+1)(x-4)=0, so A=(-1,0), B=(4,0). Let x=0, obtaining C=(0,-4). Line BC passes through (4,0) and (0,-4), and its slope is 1, so its equation is y=x-4. Let P=(t,t^2-3t-4). Because P is in the fourth quadrant and the vertical line must intersect segment BC, take 0<t<4. The vertical line through P is x=t, so Q is on BC, Q=(t,t-4). Thus PQ=(t-4)-(t^2-3t-4)=-t^2+4t=-(t-2)^2+4. Therefore the maximum value of PQ is 4, at this time t=2. Substituting into the parabola, P=(2,2^2-3·2-4)=(2,-6).
